verdict: Meta's revenue jumped 22% to $47.5B as its ads reached more people at higher prices — and with costs growing only half as fast, it kept $18.3B as profit, about 39 cents of every dollar.

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: after $17.0B of capex incl. finance leases

kpis.label: Family DAP
kpis.note: people using Meta's apps daily, +6% YoY

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Ads across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger: impressions rose 11% and the average price per ad rose 9%.

segments.name: Family of Apps other revenue
segments.note: WhatsApp business messaging, Meta Verified subscriptions and other app income; up 50% YoY.

segments.name: Reality Labs
segments.note: Quest headsets and AI glasses; revenue rose 5% and the unit lost $4.5B this quarter.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: AI research, engineers and Reality Labs development; up 23% YoY.

opex.name: Marketing & sales
opex.note: Selling ads and marketing Meta's apps and devices.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Back-office and legal costs — well down from $3.7B a year ago.

follow100Note: Advertising is $97.99 of every $100 Meta takes in. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
otherDetail: Meta reports one combined line, interest and other income (expense), net; this quarter it was a $93M net gain.

takeaways.title: The ad engine is running hot
takeaways.text: Ad impressions rose 11% and the average price per ad rose 9%, powered by AI ad tools — advertising brought in $46.6B of the $47.5B total.

takeaways.title: Margins widened sharply
takeaways.text: Operating margin reached 43%, up from 38% a year ago, because revenue grew 22% while total costs grew only 12%.

takeaways.title: Reality Labs still burns cash
takeaways.text: The headsets-and-glasses unit lost $4,530M in one quarter on just $370M of revenue — the price Meta pays to build its next platform while the ad business funds it.
